subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope and acceptance bar should this native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency investigation use: a public runbook, new instrumentation spans, measured code fixes, or a staged combination?
rationale: The repository already has broad observability primitives, but the issue asks for measurement synthesis across many runtime and host layers, so automation cannot safely choose the measurement environment or done criteria.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a focused native-Linux Gateway performance runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and lists measured gaps before code changes.

options.title: Sponsor instrumentation PRs first
options.body: Pick the missing spans or timing fields maintainers want and split them into narrow PRs before writing an end-to-end analysis.

options.title: Leave as support-only
options.body: Keep the issue as operator guidance and ask for reporter-supplied traces before investing core/docs work.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a focused native-Linux Gateway performance runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and lists measured gaps before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Most current code and docs evidence for the affected performance, diagnostics, context, and gateway surfaces routes through Peter Steinberger.
